title: Know Your Numbers
hook: A handful of routine numbers — blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, and waist size — quietly predict much of your future health, and most have no symptoms until something breaks.
key_points: Key numbers: blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, and BMI or waist size.
Most carry no symptoms, so testing is how you actually know where you stand.
Normal blood pressure is generally under 120/80 mm Hg.
Healthy targets vary by person; your clinician sets goals for your situation.
Knowing your numbers lets you act early, when changes work best.
content_html: A small set of numbers tells you a surprising amount about your long-term health — and the trouble is that high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and rising blood sugar usually announce nothing at all until they've already caused harm. Knowing where you stand is how you get ahead of them.
extra_html: The American Heart Association points to a core group of measures worth tracking: blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, and body weight or waist size. Normal blood pressure is generally below 120/80 mm Hg, and your clinician can interpret the others in light of your age, history, and overall risk. The exact targets are individualized — what counts as a healthy goal for one person may differ for another — which is why these numbers are best reviewed with a professional rather than judged against a single cutoff. The real payoff is timing: catching a number drifting in the wrong direction early gives lifestyle changes and, if needed, treatment the best chance to work.

related.title: Understanding Blood Pressure
related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

related.title: Understanding Cholesterol
related.hook: Cholesterol has a good side and a bad side. Too much of the bad kind builds up in your arteries for years — silently — until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

related.title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

related.title: Keeping Your Heart Healthy
related.hook: Most heart disease isn't bad luck — it's the sum of a few everyday habits. The American Heart Association distills them into eight that move the needle most.

flashcards.back_html: Blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, and BMI or waist size — together they capture much of your cardiovascular and metabolic risk.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the AHA emphasize testing rather than waiting for symptoms?

flashcards.explanation_html: Risk factors such as high blood pressure and high cholesterol typically cause no symptoms, so measuring them is the only reliable way to know your status.
